jobs.title: Executive Director, Global Regulatory Change Management and Program Delivery
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

CIBC’s Capital Markets business is committed to being the premier client-focused Capital Markets group in Canada, offering a comprehensive suite of credit, capital markets, investment banking, merchant banking, and research products and services to government, institutional, corporate, and retail clients both domestically and internationally.

As the Executive Director, Global Regulatory Change Management and Program Delivery, reporting to the Managing Director, you will be responsible for leading the Capital Markets Global Regulatory program and project delivery team. You will be accountable for overseeing a portfolio of planned and in-flight regulatory changes ensuring appropriate funding, resourcing and escalation of risks when required. You will also be accountable for leading a project delivery practice that includes both business and regulatory changes. You will manage and oversee the program financials for the Capital Markets Compliance programs, creating governance arrangements from the inception of new changes through the impact assessment and financial planning process. You will identify and engage key stakeholders across the enterprise to ensure alignment, collaboration and transparency. You will lead a project and program delivery practice accountable for delivery regulatory and business changes across Capital Markets. You will build out the consistent application of tools, frameworks and techniques for initiating, planning, organizing, monitoring and controlling projects with a focus on financial and schedule management and demonstrate creative problem-solving skills by thriving in ambiguity, connecting the dots and driving continuous improvement.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How You’ll Succeed

Regulatory Program Financial Management – You will manage and oversee the program financials by adopting a comprehensive and holistic approach the encompasses all aspects of the program. You will establish adequate governance and controls around one-time expenditures and new ongoing costs, ensuring appropriate levels of transparency throughout the process. Additionally, you will implement strategies to control spending while collaborating with partners to allocate resources effectively, promoting financial responsibility and efficiency.
Regulatory Change Governance & Strategy Leader – You will oversee Regulatory Change Management governance, initiatives and delivery be designing and coordinating the global intake process for all potential regulatory changes impacting Capital Markets. You will ensure a thorough impact assessment of changes from business, technology and change management perspectives. You may act as a representative of Regulatory Change Management on industry regulatory forums.
Regulatory Planning – As part of regulatory change planning, you will be responsible for appropriate and accurate financial planning. You will promote transparency regarding the global pipeline by coordinating and leading governance forums such as management and executive steering committees. You will be accountable for the accuracy of the materials presented, ensuring that key regulatory topics and risks are surfaced appropriately.
Regulatory Management & Support – You will provide essential support for “Business as Usual” regulatory matters impacting Capital Markets, including regulatory examinations and internal audits. You will also assist with ad hoc ongoing activities necessary to ensure regulatory compliance for Capital Markets, contributing to the overall effectiveness and integrity of the regulatory framework. Additionally, you will work with the Global Regulatory Chane Management Group and key stakeholders to develop Senior Management presentations and updates for regulatory change initiatives as well as governance updates for Capital Markets and Regulatory Enterprise committees.
Project & Program Delivery – You will lead a project and program delivery practice accountable for end-to-end delivery of business and regulatory projects and programs. This includes project initiation, planning, scheduling, funding request development, governance management and ensure all projects adhere to the Enterprise Delivery Framework. You’ll build out a consistent approach and framework to deliver change at an accelerated pace, documenting best practices in playbooks. You will integrate AI across the delivery lifecycle to help accelerate project artifact generation, schedule creation and monitoring, project logs, etc.
Leading a High-Performing Team – You will establish and communicate a clear vision and objectives for the team, ensuring alignment with the broader organizational and business strategy. You will focus on team and talent management by implementing effective performance management strategies and establishing clear performance goals and expectations for your team members. You will ensure a system for regular, ongoing feedback to support your team’s development and growth and provide regular, ongoing feedback. By fostering a positive culture, you will create an inclusive and supportive work environment that encourages idea generation, collaboration and innovation.
Relationship Management – You will create a positive work environment and serve as an effective role model by championing CIBC’s mission, vision and values. You will establish and maintain strong working relationships with counterparts across business units within CIBC, facilitating the execution of efficient and proactive change in areas such as Compliance, Finance, Legal, Supervision and Governance, Technology and Operations. Additionally, you will remain accessible to the business throughout the day, actively responding to requests in a timely manner to support collaboration and effectiveness.

Who You Are

You have extensive industry experience. You bring 10 years of financial services expertise to the role, along with a strong understanding of CIBC’s operating policies, standards, and organizational structure. You have a good understanding of Capital Markets and experience delivering Capital Markets-wide projects.
You have deep project and program delivery experience. You have expertise in delivering projects and programs within Capital Markets.
You have Undergraduate degree. In business and/or an equivalent field/area.
You’re a strong communicator. You use your excellent communication and interpersonal skills to build, manage, and leverage relationships with colleagues at all levels, as well as internal and external business partners.
You have the knowledge of the operational, regulatory, and reputation risks. Within the capital markets environment and comprehension of the policies, standards, processes and controls that need to be in place to mitigate these risks.
You thrive in fast-paced environments. You’re comfortable managing multiple priorities and consistently deliver high-quality work even when faced with tight deadlines.
You’re a process innovator. You excel at establishing key processes in areas where guidelines may not yet exist, and you proactively initiate design and development to create effective workflows. You continuously seek opportunities to improve and refine processes, enhancing efficiency and effectiveness across the team.
You’re a strategic problem solver. You bring strong analytical skills and sound judgment to complex situations, enabling you to implement effective changes.
You’re a self-starter. You take initiative, work independently, and consistently demonstrate ownership of your responsibilities. Your results-oriented approach helps you achieve goals and drive success.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose
, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province. We are energized to grow
, embracing opportunities to shape the future of a dynamic and evolving energy sector while advancing our careers. We are powered by teamwork
, supported by diverse and passionate colleagues who foster respect, celebrate successes, and thrive on shared achievements. At the IESO, it’s not just what we do— it’s who we are!

Who We Are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a non-unionized position that falls within the Markets and Reliability Business Unit.

What Makes This Role Exciting

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

As part of the recent Markets and Reliability (M&R)
reorganization, designed to improve efficiency and ways of working, the former System Integration
division has been renamed Power System Integration
.

A new Director, Engineering Studies
position has been created to lead a centralized centre of expertise, bringing together engineering and power system study functions from across M&R, including WINTOP, Operability, Connection Assessments, and Power System Limits. The successful candidate will provide strategic leadership for these functions and play a key role in change management and the transition to the new organizational structure.

Reporting to the Sr Director, Power System Integration and managing a team of direct and indirect reports, the Director, Engineering Studies provides senior management oversight and leadership to deliver Divisional initiatives.

The Director, Engineering Studies is responsible for overseeing the execution of engineering studies that support the connection process, operational planning, real-time operations and other initiatives, as needed, within the IESO. They provide input on the strategic direction as it relates to the Division’s scope and work to align the Division’s strategies with those of the Business Unit and the IESO's overall strategic objectives.

They are responsible for supporting their leader and setting strategic direction for their Division. Where relevant, they are responsible for developing a plan or approach that connects their Division to the IESO’s strategic goals, ensuring their Division deliver results, and that their staff are set up for success.

The Director role is responsible to define division level objectives that directly support Business Unit level goals and Corporate Performance Measures. As well, the role is responsible for input and ownership of elements of the Strategy Implementation Plan and for defining metrics for their Division that align and ladder up to the BU KPIs.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:

Functional/Technical

Acts as the VP/Sr Director delegate on some internal IESO committees.
Ability to assume the signing authority and represent the VP/Sr. Director as required.
Develops and leads practices for their Division that may have organizational-wide impact including methodologies, standards, and analytical approaches for power system studies supporting grid connections, operational planning, real-time system operations and other IESO initiatives, as needed.
Defines future state goals or outcomes for their Division using general precedents or by adapting current processes and practices.

Stakeholder/Governance

May act as an external ambassador, spokesperson and facilitator for the IESO with relevant external partners to execute industry decisions/changes in the areas of connecting to the grid, power system planning and operations and, more broadly, the evolving technical requirements of the electricity system as the sector moves to its desired future state.
Has occasional interaction with IESO Executive Leadership Team and Board of Directors on connection feasibility, power system evolution, the technical capabilities and limitations of the electricity grid, significant reliability events, and emerging risks affecting system reliability and operability.
Develops and monitors risk mitigation plans on behalf of their Division regarding emerging threats to the reliability and operability of the electricity grid resulting from the rapid growth of large loads, inverter-based resources, distributed energy resources, and aggregators, as well as evolving system conditions such as increasing interdependence with gas and telecommunication and extreme weather events, a few of which may be reported to the Board of Directors; errors or failure of mitigation actions may lead to loss of reputation with relevant stakeholders

People Leadership

Provides leadership for a team of direct and indirect reports creating a working environment that is aligned with the organization’s values, ensuring that people resources possess the required skills, are properly aligned, and are provided with the resources to do the job
Provides leadership oversight and direction to staff (e.g. defines team member roles, responsibilities, and expectations); delivers timely feedback to ensure a cohesive operational unit and the optimum use of team skills; manages staff and monitors work assignments for adherence to timelines
Manages and directs cross-functional teams to deliver Divisional projects (e.g. defines team member roles, responsibilities, and expectations); delivers timely feedback to ensure cohesive teams and the optimization of team skills; oversees work assignments for adherence to timelines and the achievement of performance objectives
Champions change leadership and provides senior level support of continued improvements and achievement of Divisional objectives
Supports workplace transformation and implementation aligned with the strategic vision, connected to and aligned with strategic corporate goals; provides leadership within the management environment
May influence objectives and plans at the corporate and BU level and cascades them to Division
Accountable for Division performance review process compliance
Provides insight and guidance to Division in calibrating performance of teams in support of fairness and equity across the IESO
Accountable for execution of strategic people leadership activities for their Division
Ensures team(s) output effectively meets business needs and goals; ensuring quality, quantity, and timeliness of work production to achieve Division’s objectives

Financial Stewardship

Participates in annual corporate-wide budgeting processes, allocates budget across teams within division, and oversees budget consumption through monitoring internal controls and safeguards to ensure Divisional budget activity is aligned to plan
Develops and manages annual and long-term budgets and staffing plans that adhere to corporate standards and applicable legislation
Monitors project and program progress to deliver objectives on time and within budget, and achieve anticipated business results while maximizing capital investment
Identifies Divisional budget needs to inform business planning
Meets service delivery objectives and manages project and Divisional activities within budgetary limits
Monitors progress to ensure that Divisional objectives are delivered on time and within budget, and that anticipated business results are achieved
Oversees relevant consultant and vendor contracts
Establishes processes, controls, and measures to ensure appropriate expense allocation, cost management, and overall fiscal responsibility
Applies LEAN principles to support financial stewardship
Develops and updates monthly reports (e.g. Business Performance Reviews and Key Performance Indicators)

In a typical day, you will lead a team of engineering and power system experts, providing strategic direction and oversight for studies that support grid connections, operational planning, reliability, and real-time system operations. You will collaborate with senior leaders, cross-functional teams, and external industry stakeholders to address emerging challenges, assess risks, and develop solutions that support a reliable and evolving electricity system. Acting as a delegate for the VP/Sr. Director when required, you will represent the division in key governance forums and contribute to critical decisions impacting system operability and future grid capabilities. You will champion organizational change, guide the implementation of new practices and methodologies, and ensure your teams deliver high-quality results that align with divisional and corporate objectives. You will also oversee budgets, resources, and project performance to ensure business goals are achieved efficiently and effectively.

Role Requirements

Our team consists of experts from diverse backgrounds, each bringing their unique perspectives and skills.

To Succeed In This Role, You’ll Need

Over 15 years’ experience in the electricity sector, addressing increasingly complex issues.
Superior communication skills, both verbal and written.
Strong strategic thinking skills with a long-term perspective.
Exceptional attention to detail.
Strong listening and stakeholder engagement skills.
Extensive knowledge of the IESO structure and mandate, and the Ontario electricity sector to support the execution of engineering studies related to the connection process, operational planning, real-time operations and other IESO initiatives.
A strong understanding of power system issues and stakeholder perspectives.
Excellent planning, organizational, and management skills, with experience managing complex and evolving priorities.
Proven experience in business strategy, leading and developing teams, developing and monitoring budgets.
Strong technical and analytical knowledge in the electricity industry, particularly in power system planning and operations.
Current knowledge of industry activities, trends, best practices and technological developments related to power system reliability and engineering study methodologies and tools.
Excellent analytical, problem solving, conceptual and forward-thinking skills.
Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization.
A professional engineering designation would be an asset.

How We Support You

From a comprehensive total rewards program to dynamic learning and development opportunities—including job rotations to broaden your expertise—we empower you to define and shape your own success. When you join the IESO, here’s what you can expect:

Best-in-class benefits and long-term support in the form of a defined benefit pension plan.
Work in a dynamic and evolving sector that offers exciting opportunities and the chance to explore new career paths.
Leadership that values meaningful discussions, welcomes feedback, and prioritizes career development.
A strong, inclusive culture and a collaborative team environment with a shared passion for impactful work.

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose
, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province. We are energized to grow

Who We Are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a non-unionized position that falls within the Markets and Reliability Business Unit.

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

As part of the recent Markets and Reliability (M&R)
reorganization, designed to improve efficiency and ways of working, the former System Integration
division has been renamed Power System Integration
.

position has been created to lead a centralized centre of expertise, bringing together engineering and power system study functions from across M&R, including WINTOP, Operability, Connection Assessments, and Power System Limits. The successful candidate will provide strategic leadership for these functions and play a key role in change management and the transition to the new organizational structure.

They provide input on the strategic direction as it relates to the Division’s scope and work to align the Division’s strategies with those of the Business Unit and the IESO's overall strategic objectives.

They are responsible for supporting their leader and setting strategic direction for their Division. Where relevant, they are responsible for developing a plan or approach that connects their Division to the IESO’s strategic goals, ensuring their Division deliver results, and that their staff are set up for success.

The Director role is responsible to define division level objectives that directly support Business Unit level goals and Corporate Performance Measures. As well, the role is responsible for input and ownership of elements of the Strategy Implementation Plan and for defining metrics for their Division that align and ladder up to the BU KPIs.

What You’ll Do

Functional/Technical

Acts as the VP/Sr Director delegate on some internal IESO committees.
Ability to assume the signing authority and represent the VP/Sr. Director as required.
Develops and leads practices for their Division that may have organizational-wide impact including methodologies, standards, and analytical approaches for power system studies supporting grid connections, operational planning, real-time system operations and other IESO initiatives, as needed.
Defines future state goals or outcomes for their Division using general precedents or by adapting current processes and practices.

Stakeholder/Governance

Champions change leadership and provides senior level support of continued improvements and achievement of Divisional objectives
